body.heading: Where in the world is Vatican City?
paragraphs: Vatican City is a country in Southern Europe, which is part of Europe.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Vatican City is Vatican City. Vatican City is a country and a city all in one — the smallest country in the world, tucked inside Rome, the capital of Italy.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: People in Vatican City speak Italian and Latin.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Vatican City is the euro. The euro is shared by many countries in Europe, so the same coins and notes work across borders.

body.heading: How big is Vatican City?
paragraphs: Vatican City covers about 0.49 square kilometres of land and inland water. It is the smallest country in the whole world — you could walk across it in about fifteen minutes.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: St Peter's is the largest church in the world, crowned by Michelangelo's dome — climb it for a view over the square's colonnades and all of Rome.
The Vatican Museums hold centuries of art, ending at the Sistine Chapel, where Michelangelo painted the most famous ceiling in the world.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Vatican City on a map or globe. Which continent is it on — and can you name a country that sits next to it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?
